module_title: Supreme Court - Judicial Review, Activism, and Special Powers
introduction: This level explores 'Judicial Review', 'Judicial Activism', Public Interest Litigation (PIL), and the extraordinary powers under Article 142 to deliver 'Complete Justice'.

core_concepts.title: Judicial Review (Article 13)
core_concepts.description: The power of the SC to examine the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders. If they violate the Constitution, the SC can declare them 'void'.

core_concepts.title: Article 142 (Complete Justice)
core_concepts.description: The SC can pass any order or decree necessary for doing 'complete justice' in any cause or matter pending before it. This power is unique and far-reaching.

core_concepts.title: Judicial Activism & PIL
core_concepts.description: Judicial activism is the proactive role played by the judiciary in protecting the rights of citizens. PIL (Public Interest Litigation) allows any public-spirited person to seek justice for the oppressed.

core_concepts.title: Curative Petition
core_concepts.description: The last legal resort for a person after a review petition is dismissed. It ensures that there is no gross miscarriage of justice (Concept evolved from the Rupa Ashok Hurra case).

core_concepts.title: Ad-hoc Judges (Article 127)
core_concepts.description: When there is a lack of quorum to hold any session, the CJI can appoint a High Court judge as an 'Ad-hoc' judge of the SC with the prior consent of the President.

important_entities.name: Justice P.N. Bhagwati
important_entities.significance: He was instrumental in introducing and popularizing Public Interest Litigation in the 1980s.

important_entities.name: NJAC (99th Amendment)
important_entities.significance: The National Judicial Appointments Commission was declared unconstitutional by the SC in 2015 to protect the 'independence of the judiciary'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The term 'Judicial Review' is NOT explicitly mentioned in the Constitution, but the power is derived from Articles 13, 32, 131-136, and 226.
Under Article 136, SLP is a discretionary power. It is NOT a right of the citizen, but a privilege granted by the Court to hear an appeal.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Consecutive articles dealing with temporary arrangements for judges in the SC.

exam_strategy_tips: Focus on Article 142 in context of recent landmark judgments (like Ayodhya or Liquor Ban cases).
Understand the distinction between 'Judicial Activism' and 'Judicial Overreach' for descriptive questions.
